unit_label: Module A: International Banking - Documentary Letters of Credit

facts.statement: UCP 600 is leaner than its predecessor, with 39 articles against 49. It was drafted by an ICC task force and consultative group and approved by the ICC Banking Commission on 25 October 2006, in force from 1 July 2007. Its articles group as: 1-5 definitions, interpretations and independence of credits from underlying contracts; 6-10 availability, expiry, obligations of issuing and confirming banks, advising and amendments; 11-17 pre-advised credits, nominated bank, reimbursement, complying presentation and original documents; 18 commercial invoice; 19-27 transport documents; 28 insurance documents; 29-33 extension, tolerance, partial and instalment drawings, hours of presentation; 34-37 disclaimers; 38-39 transferability and assignment of proceeds. DOCDEX (Documentary Credit Dispute Resolution Expertise) is one way to resolve credit disputes.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 99-100, section 4.5 A and B

facts.statement: UCP 600 does not apply to a credit by default: the credit must state that it is subject to UCP 600, and Article 1 lets the parties exclude any part of it if the exclusion is stated.

Article 2 defines a credit as an arrangement that is irrevocable and a definite undertaking of the issuing bank to honour a complying presentation; Article 3 says a credit is irrevocable even if there is no indication to that effect; Article 10 says a credit can be neither amended nor cancelled without the agreement of the issuing bank, the confirming bank and the beneficiary. The beneficiary should notify acceptance or rejection of an amendment; if it does not, a presentation that complies with the credit and with any not yet accepted amendment is deemed to be notification of acceptance of that amendment, and from that moment the credit is amended.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 100-101, points C2 and C6

facts.statement: Articles 7 and 8 give a definite undertaking by the issuing and confirming banks to reimburse the nominated bank at maturity, whether or not the nominated bank prepaid or purchased its own acceptance or deferred payment undertaking before maturity. Under Article 9(b) an advising bank must certify that the credit it advises reflects the terms of the credit it received, and the obligation extends to a second advising bank.
facts.locator: Printed p. 100, points C4 and C5

facts.statement: Under UCP 600 a bank has a maximum of five banking days following the day of presentation to honour or refuse (UCP 500: reasonable time not exceeding seven). A banking day is a day on which a bank is regularly open at the place where an act subject to the rules is to be performed. The period for presentation, usually 21 days, applies to original transport documents; where no transport document is required the credit should state a period for presentation. Data in a document, read in context with the credit, the document itself and international standard banking practice, need not be identical but must not conflict with data in that document or any other stipulated document. Conditions in the credit that are not part of a required document are non-documentary and are disregarded.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 101-102, points C7 to C10

facts.statement: A presentation is complying when the issuing or nominated bank determines that it is, and that is when settlement begins. For discrepant documents the bank may hold them pending further instructions from the presenter; hold them until it receives a waiver from the applicant and agrees to accept it, or further instructions from the presenter before agreeing to accept a waiver; return them; or act on instructions previously received from the presenter. There is no provision for payment under reserve or indemnity.
facts.locator: Printed p. 101, points C11 and C12

facts.statement: Under UCP 600 an original document is one bearing an apparently original signature, mark, stamp or label of the issuer, or appearing to be written, typed, perforated or stamped by the issuer, or on the issuer's original stationery, or stating that it is original. A charter party bill of lading may be signed by the charterer. Transport documents no longer need to bear the clause "clean". Insurance documents providing wider coverage than stipulated are acceptable, percentage cover is a minimum, and the document may refer to an exclusion clause. If the nominated bank determines that a presentation complies and forwards documents, the issuing bank must honour or reimburse even if the documents are lost in transit. A bank will not honour a credit that expired during a force majeure. A presentation by a second beneficiary under a transferable credit must be made to the transferring bank.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 102-103, points C13 to C19

facts.statement: The applicant must give complete and precise instructions and must not include excessive detail; it should indemnify banks against obligations imposed by foreign laws. The issuing bank should assure itself of the applicant's creditworthiness, gives a definite undertaking, examines documents with reasonable care to see whether they appear on their face to comply, and must refuse within five banking days; if it refuses it must say whether documents are held pending instructions or returned. The advising bank may choose whether to advise; if it does, it must take reasonable care of authenticity, and if it cannot establish authenticity it must inform the issuing bank and the beneficiary. A confirming bank that will not confirm must tell the issuing bank without delay. The negotiating bank negotiates only if documents appear on their face to comply. The reimbursing bank reimburses on receiving authorisation from the issuing bank, under URR 725. The beneficiary cannot rely on the contract between the banks or between the applicant and the issuing bank.

Banks assume no liability for the genuineness of documents; for delay or loss in transmission of messages or documents; for errors in translation or interpretation of technical terms; for interruption of business caused by acts of God, riots, civil commotions or other causes beyond their control; or for the acts of correspondent banks chosen by the applicant or by themselves. The applicant is liable for charges if the third party's charges cannot be collected, and for acts done or losses occurring because of foreign laws.

payload.title: UCP 600 as a map: 39 articles in nine groups
payload.core_explanation_md:
UCP 600 trimmed the rulebook from **49 articles to 39**. A map of the groups is more useful than memorising numbers.

- **1-5**: definitions, interpretations, and that the credit is **independent** of the underlying contract
- **6-10**: availability, expiry, what the **issuing** and **confirming** banks undertake, **advising**, **amendments**
- **11-17**: pre-advised credits, **nominated bank**, **reimbursement**, **complying presentation**, **original documents**
- **18**: commercial **invoice**
- **19-27**: **transport** documents
- **28**: **insurance** documents
- **29-33**: extension of expiry, **tolerance**, partial and instalment drawings, hours of presentation
- **34-37**: **disclaimers** (what banks are not responsible for)
- **38-39**: **transferability** and **assignment of proceeds**

Two more facts: UCP 600 applies **only if the credit says it is subject to it** (and parties may exclude parts if stated), and **DOCDEX** is the ICC's dispute resolution route for credit disputes.

payload.title: Irrevocable by default, and how an amendment gets accepted
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Irrevocable by default.** UCP 600 defines a credit as irrevocable. A credit is irrevocable even if it does not say so (Article 3), and the old notion of a **revocable** credit disappeared in 2007. A prudent seller still asks in the sales contract for an **irrevocable** credit.

**Amendments.** A credit cannot be amended or cancelled without the agreement of the **issuing bank**, the **confirming bank** (if any) and the **beneficiary** (Article 10).

What if the beneficiary says nothing? If it presents documents that comply with the credit **and** with any amendment it has **not yet accepted**, that presentation is **deemed to be notice of acceptance** of the amendment, and from that moment the credit is amended.

So silence is not acceptance, but **acting on the amendment is**.

payload.title: Examining documents: five banking days and what to do with a discrepancy
payload.core_explanation_md:
**The clock.** A bank has up to **five banking days following the day of presentation** to decide whether to honour or refuse. (UCP 500 gave a reasonable time of up to seven.) A **banking day** is a day on which the bank is **regularly open** where the act is to be done.

**The presentation period.** Documents must usually be presented within **21 days** of shipment, but this applies to **original transport documents**. If no transport document is required, the credit should state its own period.

**What counts as a discrepancy.** Data need **not be identical** across documents, but must **not conflict**. **Non-documentary conditions** (conditions not tied to a required document) are **disregarded**.

**When a bank refuses**, it can: hold the documents pending the presenter's instructions; hold them until the **applicant waives** the discrepancy and the bank agrees to accept; return them; or act on instructions previously given. There is **no payment under reserve or indemnity**.

payload.title: Who owes what: a duty ledger for each party
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Party | Core duty |
| --- | --- |
| **Applicant** | Gives **complete, precise** instructions; avoids **excessive detail**; **indemnifies** banks against obligations imposed by **foreign laws**; pays charges that a third party does not |
| **Issuing bank** | Assures itself of the applicant's **creditworthiness**; gives a **definite undertaking**; examines documents with **reasonable care**; refuses within **five banking days** and says whether documents are **held** or **returned** |
| **Advising bank** | May choose whether to advise; if it does, checks **authenticity** with reasonable care; if unable to, tells the **issuing bank and the beneficiary** |
| **Confirming bank** | Adds its **own** undertaking; if it will not confirm, tells the issuing bank **without delay** |
| **Negotiating bank** | Negotiates only if documents **appear on their face** to comply |
| **Reimbursing bank** | Reimburses on the issuing bank's **authorisation**, under **URR 725** |
| **Beneficiary** | Cannot rely on the contract **between the banks** or between the applicant and the issuing bank |

payload.title: What banks do not answer for
payload.core_explanation_md:
UCP 600 keeps banks out of problems they cannot control. A bank does **not** take responsibility for:

- the **genuineness** of the documents (it examines them on their face)
- **delay or loss** of messages or documents in transmission
- **errors in translating or interpreting** technical terms
- **interruption of business** by acts of God, riots, civil commotion and similar causes (so a credit that **expires during a force majeure** is **not** honoured later)
- the **acts of correspondent banks**, whether the applicant or the bank chose them

And the applicant is liable for **charges** a third party does not pay, and for losses arising from **foreign laws**.

The common thread: banks answer for **reasonable examination**, not for outcomes that depend on the world outside the documents.

payload.title: Smaller changes that UCP 600 made, and the reasons for them
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **Deferred payment and acceptance** (Arts 7, 8, 12(b)): the issuing and confirming banks must **reimburse the nominated bank at maturity**, even if it prepaid or purchased early.
- **Advising** (Art 9(b)): the advising bank certifies that its advice **reflects the credit it received**, and so does any **second** advising bank.
- **Original documents** (Art 17): a document is original if it **looks** original, for example bears an apparently original signature, mark, stamp or label, or says it is original.
- **Transport**: a **charter party** bill of lading may be signed by the **charterer**; transport documents **no longer need the word "clean"**.
- **Insurance** (Art 28): **wider** cover than asked is acceptable; the stated percentage is a **minimum**; an **exclusion clause** may be mentioned.
- **Lost in transit** (Art 35): if the nominated bank has determined the presentation complies and forwarded the documents, the issuing bank must **honour or reimburse** even if they are lost on the way.
- **Transferable credits** (Art 38): a **second beneficiary** presents to the **transferring bank**.

payload.title: Counting the days: presentation deadline and the refusal deadline
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: goods are shipped on Thursday 4 June 2026 and the credit is available until 30 June 2026. The exporter presents compliant-looking documents to the nominated bank on Wednesday 24 June 2026. Assume Monday to Friday are banking days with no holidays. What is the last day for presentation, and by what date must the issuing bank decide on documents presented on 24 June?

worked_steps.description: Presentation period for original transport documents.
Also respect the expiry of the credit.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: 25 June 2026 is the last day to present

worked_steps.description: The refusal clock starts the day after presentation. Count banking days after Wednesday 24 June: Thursday, Friday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Last day to present: 25 June 2026. The issuing bank must decide within five banking days following presentation, that is by 1 July 2026

self_check.prompt_text: If the exporter had presented on Friday 26 June instead, would the presentation still have been on time, and why?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the 21 days from shipment ended on 25 June, so a presentation on 26 June is late even though the credit has not yet expired.

options.explanation_md: It does not affect irrevocability.

unresolved: The courseware lists the UCP revision years inconsistently (printed p. 89: 1951, 1962, 1974, 1983, 1993, 2007; printed p. 99: 1951, 1962, 1984, 1994, 2007 as "six times"). The items use the earlier list, which matches the standard ICC history.

The courseware cites some article numbers loosely (for example the applicant's indemnity is given as Article 18); items teach the duties and cite article numbers only where the courseware and UCP 600's structure agree.
UCP 600 itself was not retrieved (ICC sells it); the articles are taught as the courseware describes them. The ICC page corroboration noted in batch B001 covers only the edition.
Documents under the credit (bill of exchange, invoice, bill of lading and so on; printed pp. 105-) and the safeguards, crystallisation and follow-up are in the next batches.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
